title: 2 Weeks in Japan With Only a Carry-On
creator: Rafa Domínguez
description:
Packing for two weeks in Japan with one 40L bag and a small daypack. Full packing list linked below.

Roamly eSIM: 15% off your first plan with code RAFA at https://roamly.com/rafa

Next video: landing in Tokyo with no paper map.

sentences.t: Okay, two weeks in Japan, one carry-on, one small backpack, and zero checked bags.
People keep telling me this is impossible, so today I'm packing it on camera so you can see exactly what goes in.
First, the bag itself.
This is a forty liter bag, which is right at the limit for most airlines, and the reason I like it is that it opens like a suitcase instead of from the top.
Top loading bags are great for hiking and terrible for hotel rooms, I will die on that hill.
Clothes next.
I'm bringing five shirts, two pants, one pair of shorts, and seven pairs of socks and underwear, and yes, I will be doing laundry.
Every hotel I booked has a coin laundry on the ground floor, and in Japan those are honestly kind of fun.
Everything goes into packing cubes, and I roll instead of fold, because rolled shirts come out less wrinkled and you can see everything at a glance.
Shoes are the hardest part.
I'm wearing my heaviest pair on the plane and packing one light pair of sneakers, and that's it.
Now, the thing I used to stress about most on trips like this was getting online the second I land.
These days I just use Roamly, which is an eSIM app, so there's no little plastic card and no line at the airport kiosk.
You pick the country, pick how much data you want, and it installs on your phone in about two minutes, before you even leave home.
When the plane touches down, you flip it on and you've got local data right away, at a fraction of what my carrier charges for roaming.
I've used it in eleven countries now, and the only time it didn't work was when I forgot to turn it on.
If you want to try it, use code RAFA at roamly.com slash rafa and you'll get fifteen percent off your first plan.
Back to the bag.
Toiletries go in one clear pouch, everything under a hundred milliliters, and I buy sunscreen when I get there because it's better in Japan anyway.
Electronics are my phone, a small power bank, one charger with two ports, and a plug converter for the stopover in Seoul on the way back.
I'm not bringing a laptop this time, which feels scary, but I want this to be a real vacation.
Then the little things that make a huge difference.
A foldable tote for groceries and souvenirs, because you will buy snacks, I promise you.
A tiny pack of laundry sheets, which weigh basically nothing.
And a coin purse, because Japan still runs on coins and your pockets will be full of them by day two.
Okay, let's see if it closes.
Come on.
There we go, with room to spare, which is good, because the snack situation on the way home is going to be serious.
Total weight, let me check, a little over nine kilos, so just under the limit for most airlines.
If you want my full packing list, it's linked down below.
Next video, we land in Tokyo and I try to find my hotel with no paper map, so wish me luck.
See you there.
